text: The OWASP Top 10 gets misread constantly as ten specific vulnerabilities a tester looks for. That's backwards. Each entry is a risk category — a bucket covering dozens of related, testable weaknesses that share a root cause. Treat it as the skeleton of your methodology inside an authorized engagement, not the whole methodology by itself.

A real report never cites a category number as the finding. It cites a specific SQL injection in a specific parameter, and then maps that back to its category for the client's risk conversation. And you don't test every category with equal depth everywhere — scope, time budget, and the application's own architecture decide where the hours go. A banking API lives or dies on access control and authentication; a static site barely has that surface at all.

Here's the current list, the OWASP Top 10:2025, which replaced the long-standing 2021 edition. A01 is Broken Access Control, which now absorbs Server-Side Request Forgery. A02 is Security Misconfiguration. A03 is Software Supply Chain Failures, a brand-new category covering your entire build and distribution pipeline. A04 is Cryptographic Failures. A05 is Injection — SQL, OS command, and cross-site scripting, anywhere untrusted input reaches an interpreter unsanitized.

A06 is Insecure Design. A07 is Authentication Failures. A08 is Software or Data Integrity Failures. A09 is Logging and Alerting Failures. And A10 is Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions — another brand-new entry, covering error states and edge cases that leak data or skip authorization checks. If your notes still reference A03 Injection or a standalone SSRF category, that's the outdated 2021 ordering.

This chapter walks through three of these categories in real depth. Lesson 18 takes Injection, A05, and turns it into actual SQL injection and cross-site scripting test cases against authorized targets. Lesson 19 covers Authentication Failures, A07, through session tokens and password reset flows. And Lesson 20 moves into the companion checklist built specifically for APIs: the OWASP API Security Top 10.

So the Top 10 is your checklist's skeleton: ten categories, each one a scoped set of concrete test cases once you know what's actually in bounds under a signed Rules of Engagement. Next lesson, we put A05 Injection to work for real, walking through how SQL injection and cross-site scripting actually behave and how you test for both without ever touching anything outside that signed scope.
